title: Half the Oxygen You Breathe Comes From Something You Can't See

scenes.text: Every second breath you take comes from the ocean.
Not from trees. Scientists estimate that at least half of the oxygen on Earth is made in the sea.
The makers are plankton, tiny floating plants and bacteria too small to see, soaking up sunlight near the surface.
One of them, called Prochlorococcus, is the smallest photosynthetic organism on Earth. On its own, it produces up to a fifth of the oxygen in the entire biosphere.
That's more than all the tropical rainforests on land, combined.
It works because the oceans cover seventy percent of the planet, and even a tiny cell, times trillions, adds up. So next time you breathe in, thank the sea. What else does the ocean do for you?

description:
Every second breath you take comes from the ocean.
NOAA estimates that roughly half of Earth's oxygen production, and some studies say 50 to 80 percent, comes from marine plankton. One tiny bacterium, Prochlorococcus, the smallest photosynthetic organism known, produces up to 20 percent of the oxygen in the biosphere, more than all tropical rainforests on land combined.
What else do you think the ocean does for you?
